name: ypproc_xfr_2_svc
prose: Handles the NIS YPPROC_XFR request (usr.sbin/ypserv/yp_server.c:318-420). It copies the transaction id into the static result and finds the caller's address. YPXFR_RETURN(CODE) (macro, lines 310-316) sets result.xfrstat = CODE, sends the RPC reply itself with svc_sendreply, calls ypxfr_callback to the caller's callback program and port, and makes the function return NULL; it is used for: yp_access refusing the map (YPXFR_REFUSED), a NULL domain (YPXFR_BADARGS), an invalid domain (YPXFR_NODOM) and a failed master lookup by ypproc_master_2_svc (logs and YPXFR_REFUSED). Otherwise it calls yp_fork. In the child (return 0) it builds the transfer arguments and execl's /usr/libexec/ypxfr (with -p yp_dir only when yp_dir is not the default); if the execl returns, the child logs and executes YPXFR_RETURN(YPXFR_XFRERR), so it sends the reply and callback and returns NULL from the handler (the _exit(0) after it is not reached). If yp_fork fails (-1) it logs and executes YPXFR_RETURN(YPXFR_XFRERR), returning NULL. In the parent it sets result.xfrstat = YPXFR_SUCC, increments the global children count and returns a pointer to the static result, so the dispatcher sends the reply. An exec failure in the child is therefore not reported through the parent's return value.
note: usr.sbin/ypserv/yp_server.c:318-420 (macro 310-316 in the same file, refusals 330-345, master 353-366, fork 368-417, child exec failure 398-399, success 413-419). Reviewer round 1 right (the error paths send the reply themselves and return NULL, not the static result); round 15 right (an exec failure happens in the child after the parent has returned success). The packet slice shows only the tail of ypproc_xfr_2_svc.
